newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia leads Helsinki up over one percent.
newsitem.headline: Nokia leads Helsinki up over one percent.

text.p: Shares closed higher on Monday with the HEX index gaining more than one percent as Nokia matched its higher New York levels and drew other shares up in its wake, brokers said.
The FOX stock futures index rose 0.92 percent to 1,071.57, while the all-share HEX advanced 1.15 percent to 3,111.21 points. Total turnover was a sturdy 640 million markka, 46 percent of it in Nokia.
Even as a higher Wall Street opening late in the session seemed to point to further upside for Finnish shares, bears warned that a downward correction could lie around the corner.
"There's no reason we should be up so high," one broker said, pointing to weakness across Europe on Monday.
Nokia gained 10.50 markka to end at 354.00 after lively 300 million markka dealings for both series of its shares.
Nokia got an extra lift in the last half hour of trade when its ADR opened steady then began to rise on Wall Street.

"The jitters over tech shares seem to have vanished," one market analyst said, adding that Nokia had also been helped by a "buy" recommendation from Salomon Brothers, which initiated coverage of Nokia on Friday.
In its bourse debut, machinery and power group Kyro closed at 38.40 markka after starting at 39.00, more than 40 percent above its offering price of 27.00 markka.
Brokers said sentiment towards the share was positive and that they expected it to find a footing near these levels.

Chemicals group Kemira ended flat at 52.40 markka after spending most of the session off slightly following its interim report, which showed January-April profits down 21 percent, but in line with analysts' forecasts.
Metal and engineering industry shares added breadth to the day's rise, with Valmet up 0.50 markka to 90.40, Rauma adding 1.00 to 121.00 and Outokumpu gaining 2.50 to 106.50 markka.
A late spurt by meteorological equipment maker Vaisala took it up 23.00 markka to 380.00 after it reported January-April profits up 38 percent.
